relations.note: Menoetius is consistently named as a son of Iapetus.
relations.date: late eighth century BCE–second century CE

relations.note: Hesiod names the Oceanid Clymene as Menoetius’s mother.
Pseudo-Apollodorus names the Oceanid Asia as Menoetius’s mother.
Menoetius is Ocean’s grandson through his Oceanid mother.
relations.date: late eighth century BCE–second century CE

relations.note: Atlas and Menoetius are sons of Iapetus; no interaction is narrated.

relations.note: Prometheus and Menoetius are sons of Iapetus; no interaction is narrated.
relations.date: late eighth century BCE–second century CE

relations.note: Epimetheus and Menoetius are sons of Iapetus; no interaction is narrated.

relations.note: Zeus strikes Menoetius with a smouldering thunderbolt and sends him into Erebus.
Zeus strikes Menoetius during the Titan battle and hurls him into Tartarus.
